newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain says holds two Qataris on spying charges.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain says holds two Qataris on spying charges.

text.p: Bahrain said on Monday it had arrested two Qataris on charges of spying, the official Gulf News Agency reported.

An official source quoted by the agency said a man and a woman had confessed before an investigating judge to spying for Qatar. They were named as Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri.
The source said they told the judge they were sent to gather information that could harm Bahrain's national security and passed it to Qatari intelligence.
Baker, who the source described as a Qatari intelligence officer, and Salwa would be tried in Bahrain, he said.
The source said the island state of Bahrain in January 1987 arrested a similar group on charges of spying for Qatar. He gave no further details.

Qatar and Bahrain are locked in a territorial dispute over a group of barren islands, reefs and sandbanks which are potentially valuable and of strategic importance. They have been controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.
Qatar, a peninsula on the east coast of Saudi Arabia, has taken the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. The move has angered Bahrain which insists on a Gulf Arab solution.
Qatar has said it would only withdraw the court case if mediation by Saudi Arabia, the region's dominant power, succeeded in solving the dispute.
Bahrain has said it will boycott this week's Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit in Qatar's capital Doha, saying Qatar has behaved in an "unfriendly" manner.
The GCC -- a political and economic alliance of Gulf Arab states -- groups Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait and Oman. The summit is due to take place from December 7-9.
